forces: Admission must be gated by an explicit bounded capacity so unbounded concurrent submission cannot cause unbounded resource use, without depending on any transport, queue, or storage runtime mechanism.
Overload must be a deterministic, immediate, synchronous outcome — never queued, never a silent drop — so a caller can rely on the result of one submit call.

Capacity accounting must never drift regardless of whether the wrapped operation succeeds or fails, and must remain correct under concurrent submission with only cooperative (non-preemptive) scheduling.
The gate must compose above any delivery mechanism (a raw handoff, a retry-wrapped delivery, or otherwise) without coupling to any one of their result shapes.

approach-alternative-implement-delivery-.reason: A buffering queue reintroduces exactly the unbounded-memory risk backpressure exists to prevent, contradicts the issue's explicit exclusion of queue capacity beyond the bound, and turns a deterministic immediate result into a delayed one the caller cannot rely on synchronously.

evidence_ids: overload-rejection test: admission at capacity returns rejected_overload synchronously without invoking the wrapped operation
concurrent-admission test: exactly `capacity` submissions proceed and every submission beyond that is rejected
release-after-completion test asserts depth returns to zero after success
release-after-failure test asserts depth returns to zero after a rejected operation, via try/finally
all-admitted-settle test: every admitted submission's own result is awaited and reported, none discarded

security_justification.audit_integrity: The module never reports an operation as admitted without actually invoking it, and never reports a result other than the wrapped operation's own settlement.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: The module performs no authentication or authorization; it gates admission by count only, independent of caller or credential identity.
security_justification.authority_provenance: The module does not read, construct, or forward any event identity; it only counts in-flight operations and forwards whatever the wrapped operation returns.
security_justification.concurrency: Admission is a synchronous check-then-increment with no `await` between them, which is atomic under Node's run-to-completion semantics; release happens in a `finally` so exactly one release occurs per admission regardless of interleaving.
security_justification.confidentiality: The module never inspects, stores, or logs the wrapped operation's arguments or result; observability hooks receive only numeric depth and capacity.
security_justification.cryptography: No cipher, key, signature, hash, or TLS configuration is introduced or touched.
security_justification.error_disclosure: A wrapped operation's rejection propagates to the caller unchanged (this module adds no error text of its own beyond its own bounded construction-time TypeError), and the overload result carries only numeric depth/capacity.
security_justification.external_security_integration: The module adds no network client, security service, credential store, or external runtime integration; it wraps a caller-supplied function.
security_justification.fail_posture: Overload fails closed immediately and synchronously rather than queueing or silently dropping; a wrapped operation's failure still releases capacity so the gate cannot wedge itself into permanent unavailability.
security_justification.lifecycle: The module holds only an in-memory counter for its own lifetime; it starts no timer, socket, interval, or background task and needs no shutdown handling of its own.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: The change is bounded to the new backpressure module, its export, tests, documentation, and the owning OpenSpec artifacts and capability specification.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: The module performs no personal-data collection, transformation, or retention; it never inspects the wrapped operation's payload.
security_justification.resource_retention: In-flight count is bounded by validated construction-time capacity (1-100,000); no operation result, argument, or timer is retained after settlement.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: The module never retries; it wraps whatever operation it is given exactly once per submit call and reports that call's own outcome.
security_justification.trust_boundary: The only attacker-controlled pressure this module answers is submission rate; concurrent excess submissions are rejected deterministically rather than admitted, queued, or silently dropped.
